signature.name: Old Jaffa
signature.detail: The ancient port quarter is Tel Aviv's most famous sight, with stone alleys, a flea market and sea views that draw every first-time visitor. Go early in the morning to beat the crowds and heat, and wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestones.

signature.name: Tel Aviv Beach
signature.detail: The long Mediterranean beachfront is the heart of the city, with calm swimming and lively promenades. Late afternoon is best for swimming and sunset; the beaches are free and easy to reach on foot or by bus.

signature.name: Neve Tzedek
signature.detail: One of the city's oldest neighborhoods, now a charming maze of restored houses, galleries and quiet lanes. Wander on a weekday morning when it is calm, and dress casually for walking.

signature.name: Carmel Market
signature.detail: The bustling open-air market is the best place to taste local food and feel the city's everyday energy. Come before noon on Friday for the fullest stalls, and bring cash for snacks.

signature.name: Bauhaus/White City architecture
signature.detail: Tel Aviv holds one of the world's great collections of Bauhaus and International Style buildings, a UNESCO-listed draw. A self-guided walk is free; start in the morning to avoid the midday sun.

signature.name: Rothschild Boulevard
signature.detail: This leafy boulevard mixes historic buildings, cafes and the story of the city's founding. It is free and pleasant to stroll in the late afternoon or evening.

signature.name: HaYarkon Park
signature.detail: The city's largest green space offers lawns, paths and river-side walks for a break from the streets. Early morning or late afternoon is coolest; entry is free.

signature.name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
signature.detail: A major museum with a strong modern and Israeli collection, worth a half day for art lovers. Check opening hours and ticket prices ahead, as some days are shorter.

transport: Bus ride about $2; taxis and rideshares moderate
